newsitem.title: USA: Electric Fuel in pact on zinc-air battery.
newsitem.headline: Electric Fuel in pact on zinc-air battery.

text.p: The Electric Power Research Institute has agreed to foster commercial introduction of Electric Fuel Corp's zinc-air battery in North America, Electric Fuel said Tuesday.
A memorandum of understanding to collaborate on development of the technology was signed following an institute study of the zinc-air technology, the company said.
Electric Fuel said its relationship with the institute -- the research and development organization for the electricity industry -- is its first entry into the U.S.
Electric Fuel said its technology has been demonstrated in Europe and is being used in a field test with Deutsche Post AG, the German postal authority.

Electric Fuel has a license agreement with Edison SpA, Italy's largest private energy supplier, to commercialize the zinc-air battery system in Italy, Spain, France and Portugal, and it recently signed a rights agreement with Vattenfall AB to build and operate the Electric Fuel infrastructure in Scandinavia.
Under the pact with the Electric Power Research Institute, Electric Fuel said, a phased joint program for the zinc-air battery system will begin shortly.

The program will assess the fleet market acceptability of the Electric Fuel zinc-air battery; investigate the economic feasibility of establishing a zinc regeneration infrastructure in specific U.S. geographic regions; assess the environmental impact of the technology and its infrastructure; verify performance of the zinc-air battery system in a certified laboratory; and test the performance of the battery under actual use conditions in the U.S.
Once these objectives are achieved, Electric Fuel and thwe institute will plan a commercialization strategy for the technology in the U.S.

The company said it and the institute expect to form alliances with public and private organizations to support the phased program and advance the commercialization of the zinc-air technology and its applications.
"This agreement is a significant milestone toward commercializing the Electric Fuel zinc-air technology in the United States," said Yehuda Harats, chief executive of Electric Fuel.
